flags.title: The Icelandic vote was for integration without membership. The reason why is Iceland’s very distinctive understanding of sovereignty
flags.summary: The Icelandic people have decided to reject the reopening of EU accession talks. With 52.8% of votes against and 47.2% in favour, the margin was narrow enough to make clear that the country is divided almost equally in two over the issue. However, the referendum hasn’t been a direct vote on future EU membership. A […]

flags.title: Iceland voted ‘no’ – what it means is that the EU failed to make its case
flags.summary: In their referendum this past weekend, Icelanders rejected resuming EU accession talks but only by a narrow margin: 52.8 % against, 47.2 % in favour. This suggests that concerns over fishing, long linked to Icelanders’ sense of national identity, ultimately prevailed at the ballot box, triumphing over existential security threats and the broader geopolitical case for Europe. flags.title: Talk is cheap: Europe’s defence promise meets the EU budget
flags.summary: At July’s NATO summit in Ankara, European leaders accepted that they must carry more of their own defence. Turning that promise into money means winning a fight over the EU’s next seven-year budget, against coalitions that have defended farm and cohesion spending for decades
